title: Algolia Analytics API key: an ACL-defined role whose sensitivity is not stated
summary: A key sent in x-algolia-api-key to the regional Analytics API hosts, accepted whenever its ACL includes the analytics permission.
rationale: Claim analytics-api-key-accepts-any-key-with-acl records that the Analytics API accepts any key whose ACL includes analytics, and claim analytics-api-key-regional-hosts records the regional hosts the key travels to. The role is therefore defined by an ACL, in a header shared with every other role. Open: whether the predefined Analytics key is a distinct credential or an ACL profile of the general key kind (open-questions 3 and 4), how sensitive the returned data is and so what handling Algolia expects (open-question-5), and any value shape (open-questions 1 and 2). Contract claims cited: analytics-api-key/analytics-api-key-accepts-any-key-with-acl, analytics-api-key/analytics-api-key-regional-hosts.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted. Settled by: an Algolia statement of the confidentiality expected for an Analytics key and of whether it is a distinct key kind.

sources.supports: x-algolia-api-key. An API key with the necessary permissions to make the request. The required access control list (ACL) to make a request is listed in each endpoint’s reference.
Use analytics API (analytics): allowed to retrieve data with the Analytics API.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. No expectation is asserted and no value was built: the record states what the cited contract settles and what it leaves open. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
